title: もう and まだ: the time relations
summary: まだ means a state still holds and a change is expected; もう means the change has already happened. Both are ways of saying now.

blocks.text: Both words are about **now**, seen against a point where things change. **まだ** (still, not yet) says: we are inside a stretch of time that began in the past and is expected to end. **もう** (already) says: the change has happened and we are in the new stretch.
**まだ** says that now is still inside the old stretch of time. The change has not come yet.
まだ: the change comes after now.

blocks.jp: 宿題はまだしていない。
blocks.en: I haven't done my homework yet.

blocks.text: With a negative, まだ becomes "not yet", but Japanese really says "still not".

blocks.jp: さくらはまだ大人ではない。
blocks.en: Sakura is not an adult yet. (still not)

blocks.text: On its own, **まだまだ** is the modest reply to a compliment: "I still have a long way to go." Denying a compliment is the polite thing to do.

blocks.en: No, not yet (I'm still far from good).

blocks.text: **もう** says that the change has already happened, and now is inside the new stretch.
もう: the change came before now.

blocks.en: I'm all right now (no more time needed).

blocks.text: Compare 今大丈夫 (fine at this moment) with もう大丈夫 (fine now, no more time needed): もう carries the nuance that something was different before.

blocks.en: I'm all right at the moment.

blocks.text: Because もう is also a kind of now, dictionaries sometimes translate it as "now". It carries the nuance that something was different before. A standalone **もう!** is exasperation, like "Enough already!"
もう: one more, soon, a little more
There is a second もう, meaning "another" or "more". It sits in front of a number or an amount, and it is used all the time.

blocks.jp: もう一度、ゆっくり話してください。

blocks.en: I want to eat one more.

blocks.text: It also builds two time words: **もうすぐ** (soon) and **もう少し** (a little more).

items: **まだ**: the present is still inside the old stretch; change is expected later.
**まだ + negative** = not yet; **まだ + positive** = still.
**もう**: the change has already happened; also "now" with a sense of contrast.
**まだまだ**: humble reply; **もう!**: exasperation.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.prompt: 「晩ごはんは食べましたか。」「いいえ、＿＿食べていません。」
questions.note: まだ + negative = not yet.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.prompt: 「晩ごはんは食べましたか。」「はい、＿＿食べました。」
questions.en: "Have you eaten dinner?" "Yes, I already have."
questions.note: もう: the change has already happened.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.prompt: 夜の十時だけど、あの店は＿＿開いている。
questions.en: It's ten at night, but that store is still open.
questions.note: まだ + positive = still.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.prompt: まだ六時なのに、父は＿＿起きている。
questions.en: It's only six, yet my father is already up.
questions.note: もう: the new stretch has begun earlier than expected.

questions.instruction: What does もう add?
options: The change has happened: (I) have no money left
questions.note: もう marks that things are different from before.

questions.instruction: What does まだ + negative mean?
questions.note: Japanese really says "still not".

questions.instruction: Someone praises your Japanese. Which is the modest reply?
questions.note: まだまだ: "I still have a long way to go".

questions.instruction: What is a standalone もう! ?
questions.note: A cry of impatience.

questions.instruction: Which sentence says "I have already finished my homework"?
options: 宿題はまだ終わっていない。
宿題はもう終わらない。
questions.note: もう + past: the change has happened.

questions.instruction: Which sentence says "The bus hasn't come yet"?
options: バスはまだ来ていない。
questions.note: まだ + negative = not yet.

questions.instruction: Tap the word that says we are still in the old stretch
questions.en: It is still raining, as it has been since yesterday.
questions.note: まだ: the old stretch has not ended.

questions.instruction: Tap the word that says the change has already happened
questions.en: My older brother is already not angry at all.
questions.note: もう marks the new stretch.

questions.note: もう comes before what has changed.

questions.note: まだ + negative = not yet.

questions.en: Please say it one more time.

questions.instruction: True or false? まだ + positive means "still".
questions.note: まだ + positive = still; まだ + negative = not yet.

questions.instruction: Why do dictionaries sometimes translate もう as "now"?
options: It is a kind of now, with a sense that things were different before
questions.note: もう carries the nuance of contrast with before.

questions.instruction: What does まだ say?
options: We are still inside a stretch of time that began in the past and is expected to end
questions.note: まだ looks forward to a change.

questions.instruction: Which word says that we have entered the new stretch?
questions.note: もう: already.

questions.instruction: Fill the gap
questions.prompt: すみません、＿＿一つください。
questions.note: もう in front of a number means "another".

questions.instruction: What does もうすぐ mean here?
questions.note: もうすぐ means soon.
